bull.t: HPC Revenue Growth And Contracted Demand
bull.b: Rapid HPC leasing growth and a long-term Anthropic contract indicate that TeraWulf is shifting toward recurring infrastructure revenue. Greater contracted utilization can improve revenue visibility, support asset financing, and create a durable platform for scaling data-center capacity over the next several quarters.

Google’s credit support and Fluor’s comprehensive EPC role strengthen the financing and construction framework for Justified. Defined milestones, procurement oversight, and performance protections can reduce execution uncertainty while helping TeraWulf convert contracted demand into operating infrastructure.

Substantial liquidity and expanded revolving capacity provide funding flexibility for committed construction, remaining investments, and interim obligations. This resource base gives TeraWulf more ability to execute contracted projects without immediately relying on equity issuance, while supporting near-term financial resilience.

bear.b: Extremely negative operating results and free cash flow show that revenue growth has not yet translated into sustainable profitability or internally funded expansion. Persistent cash consumption can increase dependence on financing, constrain capital allocation, and magnify the consequences of weaker execution or project delays.

Large committed and remaining capital needs raise execution and funding demands even as the company continues expanding its infrastructure platform. High capital intensity can delay cash-flow breakeven, increase financing exposure, and leave less flexibility to absorb cost overruns or changes in project timing.

Muskie’s growth outlook depends on securing a customer and obtaining approval for additional generation capacity. Until those milestones are completed, planned power expansion may not convert into contracted revenue on schedule, creating uncertainty around utilization, financing needs, and returns on development spending.
